title: Aamir Khan Is Getting Married Again. This Time, He Says, He Got It Right.
excerpt: The actor has confirmed a July 5 wedding with Gauri Spratt — a Bengaluru woman he has known for 25 years and fallen in love with after two divorces, three children, and a long stretch of therapy.
body:
There is a certain kind of Bollywood love story that only works when the star is old enough to have stopped performing it. **Aamir Khan** just gave us one.

Speaking to *Variety India* this week while traveling in the United States, the 61-year-old actor confirmed what gossip columns had been circling for days: he will marry **Gauri Spratt** on **July 5, 2026**, in a private ceremony attended only by family and close friends.

> "I'm currently traveling in the US. The news about the marriage is true. It's on July 5." — Aamir Khan to Variety India

No venue announcement. No designer lehenga leak. No PR-managed countdown. Just a man on the phone, confirming that he is ready.

## The 25-Year Backstory Nobody Saw Coming

Aamir and Gauri's story reads less like a Bollywood script and more like the kind of thing that happens quietly in real life. The two first met roughly **25 years ago** through mutual connections in **Bengaluru**, where Gauri was building a career in the wellness and beauty industry. They stayed in touch casually, drifted apart entirely, and then reconnected in early 2024 through a family connection.

What began as catching up turned into something deeper. By the time Aamir introduced Gauri publicly — at his 60th birthday celebration in March 2025, during the press run for *Sitaare Zameen Par* — they had been together for over a year.

"She met Shah Rukh Khan and Salman Khan last night," Aamir told reporters at the time, grinning. "I thought it would be a nice occasion for you all to meet her, besides we won't have to keep hiding."

Gauri, who has a son from a previous relationship, was already integrated into his life. She had joined **Aamir Khan Productions** and was a quiet, steady presence at screenings and dinners. The relationship was never hidden — just never performed.

## Two Marriages, Two Lessons

This will be Aamir's **third marriage**. He married childhood sweetheart **Reena Dutta** in 1986; they divorced in 2002 after 16 years and two children — **Junaid** and **Ira Khan**. He then married filmmaker **Kiran Rao** in 2005, a union that produced their son **Azad** and ended amicably in 2021.

Both separations were handled with unusual grace for Bollywood. No tabloid wars. No custody battles in the headlines. Kiran Rao and Aamir continue to co-parent Azad and have spoken warmly about each other in public.

But Aamir has also been open about the emotional cost. In a now-widely-quoted podcast appearance with **Raj Shamani**, the actor said: "Before I met Gauri, I felt like I had aged, and who will I find at this age. Also, my therapy started, and I understood that I need to love myself first and make myself healthy. So, I worked on that."

Therapy. Self-work. A willingness to say he had been broken. It is not the kind of thing Indian superstars typically volunteer in public, and it landed.

## Why He Changed His Mind About Marriage

As recently as a few months ago, Aamir had told interviewers that marriage was not a priority — that he and Gauri were happy living together and did not need to formalize anything. When *Variety India* asked about the shift, he was direct.

> "Yes, that is true. But now we both feel we are ready to take our relationship to the next level. I am at peace. Gauri and I are serious about each other and we are in a very committed space. We are partners, we are together. In my heart, I'm already married to her. So, to formalize our togetherness just seems like a natural progression of our partnership."

The ceremony, per multiple reports, will be an **intimate court marriage** — no Bollywood spectacle, no destination wedding, no 47-page *Vogue* spread. Just a legal commitment between two people who have already committed.

## What This Means for the Diaspora

For **NRI audiences** who grew up watching Aamir reinvent Indian cinema — from *Lagaan* to *Dangal* to *3 Idiots* — the wedding carries a particular resonance. Here is a man who has been public about failure, about starting over, about the unsexy work of therapy and self-repair. And here he is, at 61, saying he feels complete.

Aamir's next film, the directorial *One Day*, is in post-production. Gauri will likely be at the premiere. And on July 5, in a room without cameras, they will make it official.

Sometimes the best love stories are the ones nobody films.
